business: Growth Buddy, a low-effort money-and-habits coach app for India
by_behaviour: Uses a free AA app already
why_not: The main thing it does for free is link my bank, and I'm not handing my account data to a brand-new app from one developer that nobody has reviewed. Without the bank link it's just another tracker I have to type into, and I've already quit two or three of those.

The only part that would make me stick with it is the bank auto-fill, and I'm not linking my bank to a brand-new app from one developer with zero reviews. Without that it's another tracker where I type stuff in, and I've quit every one of those inside two weeks.

Honestly I'd maybe download the free version if the bank linking really fills everything in, but I've quit every tracker within two weeks, so paying for Pro before I even know I'll still be opening it is not happening. My PhonePe history already tells me where the money went when I bother to look.

I've already installed Walnut, Money Manager and a habit tracker and dropped all of them within a few weeks, so I'm not paying for another one. At most I'd try the free version, and honestly one app for money, habits, health and food sounds cluttered to me.

I've never kept a budget and I just check my UPI history when money feels tight, so I might try the free version at most. AI photo estimates and a coach chat aren't things I'd pay for, and one app for money, habits, health and food sounds cluttered.

I already have Fold and INDmoney pulling my bank spends through AA for free, and I barely open those. Paying 99 a month for AI photos and a coach chat on top of a tracker I would also ignore makes no sense to me.
flip: If the free version showed me, without any effort from me, exactly where my salary goes between the 1st and the 20th and that actually helped me save, I'd consider paying for Pro, as long as there were solid reviews or some proof it's safe.
If it actually cut my Swiggy and Zomato spending in a visible way within the free version first, like showing me I saved a couple of thousand in a month, I might try Pro.
